chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Is it not pleasing to one of you that he rises before dawn, prays the Witr prayer, prays the two rak'ahs of Fajr, and it is recorded for him as the prayer of the night?'

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ: The two rak'ahs of Fajr (voluntary pre-dawn prayers)
key_terms.يُوتِرَ: To pray the Witr prayer (odd-numbered prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for praying Witr and the two voluntary rak'ahs of Fajr before dawn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the immense spiritual reward of combining the Witr prayer with the two voluntary rak'ahs of Fajr, equating this specific combination to the entirety of the night prayer (Qiyam al-Layl). This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of worship from the night into the dawn, reinforcing the concept that consistent, structured voluntary acts are highly valued in cultivating spiritual discipline and divine proximity.
